precepts.text: Then wrought Bezaleel and Aholiab and every wise hearted man in whom the Lord put wisdom and understanding; the two led a team whose hearts stirred them up to come unto the work.
precepts.point: With Aholiab of Dan and every wise-hearted man he made the tabernacle, the ark, the mercy seat, the furniture, the candlestick, the altars, the laver, the garments of Aaron and his sons, the anointing oil and the incense; we read of these things without asking who made them, and Exodus 37 lists each in detail.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
The Lord called Bezaleel the son of Uri of the tribe of Judah and filled him “with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship”. A goldsmith, a silversmith, a brass worker, a stone cutter, a wood carver: one man. And with him Aholiab of the tribe of Dan, a partner.

Here is the work being done: “Then wrought Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whom the Lord put wisdom and understanding to know how to work all manner of work for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that the Lord had commanded.”

Those two were the main men, and they had a team under them to create these things. “And Moses called Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whose heart the Lord had put wisdom, even every one whose heart stirred him up to come unto the work to do it”.

We read of the tabernacle, the ark, the mercy seat, the furniture, the candlestick, the altars, the laver, the clothes of service, the holy garments tailored for Aaron, the anointing oil and the incense, and never realize who was behind making them. They did not fall out of the sky. Somebody made every one of them: our forefathers, filled with the wisdom of the Most High. Exodus 37:1-29 gives exactly what they made, in detail.

That is the superiority of the chosen people. The Bible means what it says: these were geniuses, and they were Israel.

precepts.text: Ye shall keep the sabbath, for it is holy unto you: the penalty written on defiling it shows how seriously the Most High takes his sign.
precepts.point: On the seventh day God ended his work which he had made, and he rested on the seventh day. The seventh day is not Sunday. Seven represents completion, perfection; hold that, because the whole class hangs on it.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Many brothers coming out of the different religions think the Sabbath is for everyone. Exodus 31 shows who it was given to, and how seriously the Most High takes it: “Ye shall keep the sabbath therefore; for it is holy unto you: every one that defileth it shall surely be put to death: for whosoever doeth any work therein, that soul shall be cut off from among his people.”

It is “holy unto you,” to Israel. And the penalty written for defiling it, death and being cut off from among his people, shows how much weight God puts on it. It is not a day to congregate and then go about our own business; doing any work on it was a matter of life and death.

That weight comes from Genesis 2:3: “God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it.” What God sanctifies, his people are not to make common.

precepts.text: It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever, a perpetual covenant. Not the nations: the children of Israel only. When Christ returns, all nations will be made to keep it, but it was created for one people.
precepts.point: On the seventh day God ended his work which he had made, and he rested on the seventh day. The seventh day is not Sunday. Seven represents completion, perfection; hold that, because the whole class hangs on it.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Who is the Sabbath for? Exodus 31:16-17: “Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever.” Not between God and the Ammonites, not between God and the white man: the children of Israel only. When Christ comes back, yes, everyone will be made to keep the Sabbath; but the Sabbath was created for one people, the Israelites.

The reason given ties it straight to Genesis 2: “for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.” The same seventh day of Genesis 2:2 is the sign of the covenant.

And it points ahead. Paul writes, “For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works,” and “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” The rest in the land under Joshua was not the true rest; there were enemies on every side. Resting from servile work on the seventh day is a similitude of the true rest: when Christ comes back and we reign with him a thousand years. That is why seven means completion, perfection.

precepts.text: There are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all, and the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.
precepts.point: The Most High still works the same way. Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks, and tech savvy, and he sets every one in the body as it pleases him; no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. All the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
The Lord filled Bezaleel “with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship”, gave Aholiab with him, and put wisdom “in the hearts of all that are wise hearted”. The Most High still works the same way.

“And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all. But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.” To one “the word of wisdom”, to another “the word of knowledge”, to another faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, discerning of spirits, tongues and interpretation: “all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will.”

Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks and tech savvy. Those are diversities of operations of the same God, and all the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

precepts.text: The body is not one member, but many; the nation cannot be all teachers.
precepts.point: The Most High still works the same way. Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks, and tech savvy, and he sets every one in the body as it pleases him; no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. All the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“For the body is not one member, but many.” The nation cannot be all teachers.

The tabernacle was not built by Moses alone; the Lord called Bezaleel to work in gold, silver, brass, stones and timber, gave Aholiab with him, and put wisdom in the hearts of all that were wise hearted. Today it is the same: carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks and the tech savvy are all members of the one body, and all the diverse gifts together build the work.

precepts.text: God hath set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.
precepts.point: The Most High still works the same way. Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks, and tech savvy, and he sets every one in the body as it pleases him; no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. All the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” The Lord called Bezaleel by name and gave Aholiab with him; they did not appoint themselves.

So no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. The Most High sets every one in the body as it pleases him, the carpenter, the plumber, the electrician, the builder, the painter, the cook, and together the diverse gifts build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

precepts.text: Every day has the same sun, but by the knowledge of the Lord some days were made high days and hallowed; the sabbath is distinguished by God, not by man.
precepts.point: Six days may work be done, but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the LORD. It is more than a day of rest and congregating; it is the sign of who Israel's God is, which is why saying the sabbath is done away takes away the very sign between Israel and God.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“Why doth one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun? By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts. Some of them hath he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them hath he made ordinary days.”

Every day has the same sun, but the sabbath is distinguished by God, not by man. “Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep: for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations”. Keeping the weekly sabbath and the feast days shows that Israel are his children and he is their God. The nations do not have this sabbath; adopted Sunday worship is not the true sabbath given to the children of Israel, for it was not hallowed by the knowledge of the Lord.

precepts.text: Kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day; this speaks to the cooking fire, not to warming the household.
precepts.point: The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ is Lord of the sabbath and brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.” This speaks to the cooking fire, not to warming the household.

Eating is allowed on the sabbath, but not cooking. No microwaving, no coffee pots, no kindling the cooking fire; the sabbath meal is leftovers or simple food prepared the day before. It is the seventh day, “the sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord”.

precepts.text: Bake that which ye will bake to day, and that which remaineth is laid up until the morning; the sabbath food is cooked the day before.
precepts.point: The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ is Lord of the sabbath and brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.”

The sabbath food is cooked the day before. What is baked and seethed is prepared and laid up, so the sabbath meal is leftovers or simple food; eating is allowed, cooking is not. That is how “in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord” is kept in the kitchen.

precepts.text: If the people of the land bring ware or victuals on the sabbath day to sell, we would not buy it of them on the sabbath, or on the holy day.
precepts.point: The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ is Lord of the sabbath and brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“And if the people of the land bring ware or any victuals on the sabbath day to sell, that we would not buy it of them on the sabbath, or on the holy day”. There is no buying or selling on the sabbath or on the holy day, so gas and food are bought before sundown.

No fishing either. What could be called work opens the door to every man excusing his trade on the sabbath, and “whosoever doeth any work in the sabbath day, he shall surely be put to death.”

precepts.text: A man is better than a sheep lifted out of the pit on the sabbath; wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.
precepts.point: The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ is Lord of the sabbath and brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out? How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.”

The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ brought grace for necessities out of our control: a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger. A man is better than a sheep lifted out of the pit; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

precepts.text: The Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day; grace covers what is out of our control, never license to sin.
precepts.point: The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ is Lord of the sabbath and brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.” Christ is Lord of the sabbath, and he brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger.

That grace is never license to sin. “every one that defileth it shall surely be put to death”: the stoning was done away in Christ, but the judgment for breaking the sabbath still stands, and people still die on the sabbath day, Friday sundown to Saturday sundown. The Most High is justified, because it is his sign between him and his people.

precepts.text: The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath; therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
precepts.point: Christians use Mark 2:27 to say the sabbath is done away, but that is not what Christ said. The sabbath was made for man, the children of Israel; man was not put on the earth for the sabbath, the sabbath was put on the earth for man, and the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath because Christ instituted it. He rested for our sakes, that we should rest after the same similitude.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
Christians use this verse to say the sabbath is done away, but that is not what Christ said. “The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.”

The sabbath was made for man, the children of Israel. Man was not put on the earth for the sabbath; the sabbath was put on the earth for man. And the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath because Christ instituted it: “in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.” He rested for our sakes, that we should rest after the same similitude, “a perpetual covenant” and “a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever”.

precepts.text: The pure candlestick with all his furniture was part of the tabernacle work; the lamps ordered on it burned before the Lord continually.
precepts.point: The children of Israel were commanded to bring pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually. Aaron ordered it from the evening unto the morning before the Lord continually, upon the pure candlestick, a statute for ever in your generations.

note.label: Leviticus 24: The Pure Oil, the Shewbread, and the Blasphemer

precepts.why:
The children of Israel were commanded to bring “pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually”, and Aaron was to “order the lamps upon the pure candlestick before the Lord continually.”

That pure candlestick was part of the tabernacle work: “the table and his furniture, and the pure candlestick with all his furniture, and the altar of incense.” The lamps Aaron ordered from the evening unto the morning burned upon it before the Lord continually, a statute for ever in your generations.

precepts.text: Two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God; Deuteronomy 4:13 is the reiteration of this, for Deuteronomy means repetition.
precepts.point: And he wrote them upon two tables of stone. The laws men call the mosaic laws did not belong to Moses; they were written with the finger of God and given to Israel by Christ, and they endure for ever.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“And he gave unto Moses, when he had made an end of communing with him upon mount Sinai, two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God.” Deuteronomy 4:13 is the reiteration of this, for Deuteronomy means repetition: “he declared unto you his covenant, which he commanded you to perform, even ten commandments; and he wrote them upon two tables of stone.”

The laws men call the mosaic laws did not belong to Moses. They were written with the finger of God and given to Israel by Christ, and they endure for ever. The ten are the umbrella over all the other commandments, the sub-laws and sub-statutes beneath them.
